name: Read Repair & Anti-Entropy
tagline: Healing divergent replicas in leaderless quorum stores using hot-path digest read repair and offline Merkle-tree anti-entropy.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of replica convergence—from blocking vs. async read repair and hinted handoff limits to Merkle-tree repairs and preventing tombstone resurrection.

spark.summary: Read repair and anti-entropy background repair heal divergent replicas in eventually consistent distributed stores—read repair fixes stale keys on the hot read path, while anti-entropy reconciles entire key ranges offline using Merkle trees.
spark.keyTakeaway: Use read repair for fast, opportunistic healing of hot keys during `QUORUM` reads, and schedule periodic Merkle-tree anti-entropy repairs (`nodetool repair`) faster than `gc_grace_seconds` (e.g., < 10 days) to prevent deleted tombstones from resurrecting.

learningJourney.title: What are Read Repair & Anti-Entropy
learningJourney.explanation:
In leaderless Dynamo-style stores (Cassandra, ScyllaDB, Riak), there is no single primary log ordering every write. When a replica misses a write during an outage, two mechanisms restore convergence:

1. **Read Repair** (hot path): On a `QUORUM` read, the coordinator fetches full data from 1 replica and cryptographic **digests** from `R - 1` replicas. If digests mismatch, it fetches full values, picks the winner, and writes it back to stale replicas.
2. **Anti-Entropy** (background): Nodes exchange **Merkle trees** (hash trees over token ranges) via `nodetool repair` to pinpoint and stream divergent cold keys in $O(\log N)$ network traffic.

learningJourney.title: Why we need Anti-Entropy (Cold Keys & Zombie Tombstones)
learningJourney.explanation: Read repair only heals *active* keys; cold keys that are rarely read rot silently. Worse, if Replica C misses a `DELETE`, and peers purge the deletion **tombstone** after `gc_grace_seconds` (default 10 days / 864,000s), a subsequent read repair sees Replica C's old live row and **resurrects the deleted record ('zombie data')** across the cluster.

ideas.title: Hinted Handoff Is Best-Effort Only
ideas.description: Coordinators buffer hints for brief outages (`max_hint_window = 3h`), but hints drop if the outage exceeds 3 hours or the coordinator crashes.

ideas.title: NTP Clock Skew Breaks LWW Repairs
ideas.description: Under Last-Write-Wins (LWW), a coordinator 2 seconds ahead stamps older writes with higher timestamps—keep chrony drift <10 ms or use version vectors.

comparison.choice: Good Candidate: Cassandra, ScyllaDB, Riak & Dynamo Rings
benefits: Heals hot keys opportunistically on read and guarantees full-ring convergence on cold data.
costs: Unthrottled full Merkle repairs saturate disk compaction and streaming bandwidth.

benefits: PostgreSQL, Spanner, and etcd replicate a strict ordered log; followers cannot silently diverge on writes.
costs: Read repair has no role in single-leader consensus.

learningJourney.title: How Sub-Range Merkle Repairs & `gc_grace_seconds` are managed
learningJourney.explanation: Never set `gc_grace_seconds = 0` on tables with `DELETE`s or TTLs, schedule automated sub-range incremental repairs (e.g., Cassandra Reaper) every 3–5 days (< `gc_grace_seconds`), and throttle `stream_throughput_outbound`.

learningJourney.explanation: Balance monotonic read guarantees against repair I/O and compaction overhead.

benefits: Guarantees monotonic reads—subsequent `QUORUM` reads immediately see the repaired winner.
costs: Adds 1 extra RTT on tail latency whenever a digest mismatch triggers full-row repair.

benefits: Hashes only newly written SSTables, cutting repair CPU and disk I/O by 80–90%.
Simple, predictable token-segment orchestration that pauses automatically if compactions spike.
costs: Re-hashes entire token range every cycle.

learningJourney.title: Production example: Sub-Range Merkle Tree Anti-Entropy with Reaper
learningJourney.explanation: A 12-node Cassandra ring (`RF=3`, `gc_grace_seconds=864000`) runs **Cassandra Reaper** to divide the token ring into small sub-ranges, builds depth-15 Merkle trees per range during off-peak hours, and streams only mismatched buckets—pausing automatically if p99 read latency or pending compactions spike.

options.text: Peers purge the deletion tombstone after `gc_grace_seconds`, so a replica that missed the delete still holds the old row and read repair propagates it back as live data
options.feedback: Correct: schedule anti-entropy repairs faster than `gc_grace_seconds` so all replicas learn about tombstones before they expire.
